messages:
Priya: Alex, saw your note in ticket #5821 — can you paste the curl you used?
Alex_Cust: Hi. Our app started getting lots of 429s ~ 11:07 UTC after your update. Here's a sample request:
Alex_Cust: curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-XXXX" -d '{"model":"rw-large", "prompt":"hi","max_tokens":64}'
Alex_Cust: Response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Alex_Cust: {"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","retry_after":20}
Priya: Thanks. Which region and org?
Alex_Cust: eu-west-1, org=acme-inc, key id ends with ...9f
Eli: I'm on it. I see a canary policy deploy to policy-service at 11:04 UTC that reduced burst_per_min from 1200 -> 300 for default tier in eu-west-1.
Jordan: That matches our deploy events. New policy tag = canary-rl-2026-03-15. Canary was intended for 5% of traffic.
Eli: We also see a backlog job flush from acme side at 11:06 that sent a few hundred queued requests, so the small canary slice hit the reduced burst and started getting quota-deny.
Priya: Repro steps for us: use their key and run a 600 reqs / 60s burst -> 429s after ~300 requests.
Eli: Log snippet from policy-eval node:
Eli: ```
[11:07:12] policy-eval: key=key-9f tier=default burst=300 used=301 -> decision=deny 429
[11:07:13] infra: region=eu-west-1 canary_tag=canary-rl-2026-03-15
```
OpsBot: Deploy notice: policy-service roll 1723 applied canary-rl-2026-03-15 -> namespace=policy-canary-eu-west-1
Priya: Proposal: rollback canary in eu-west-1, then re-run canary with higher burst or narrower routing.
Jordan: Agreed. Eli, can you do immediate rollback and push emergency patch to restore previous burst=1200 for that canary?
Eli: On it. Rolling back policy-service in the canary namespace now.
Eli: kubectl -n policy-canary-eu-west-1 replace -f policy-default.yaml  # set burst_per_min=1200
OpsBot: Rollback triggered by Eli at 11:14 UTC. job_id=rb-985
DeployBot: policy-service: rollout/finalized canary-rl-2026-03-15 -> reverted to policy-v1
Priya: After rollback, Alex, could you retry the same batch? We expect relief but you may see short cold-cache rate blips.
Alex_Cust: Retried at 11:16 — much better now, only a couple of sporadic 429s. Looks resolved from our side.
Priya: Notes / action items: 1) reduce canary exposure for burst-sensitive tiers to 1% by default, 2) add synthetic burst simulation step to canary pipeline that mimics customer burst profiles, 3) update rollout checklist to require gating on "burst_simulation_passed".
Jordan: Also add an automatic short-lived circuit that temporarily raises burst window when we detect a backlog flush pattern to avoid self-inflicted outages.
Priya: Filing follow-up ticket INF-2379 with forensic logs, rollout timeline, and checklist updates. Tagging @eng-sre cohort for postmortem.
Eli: Billing note: this was quota exhaustion due to policy change, not a billing duplicate-charge issue.
BillingBot: Confirmed: no duplicate charges observed for the requests that returned 429.
Priya: I'll update the customer ticket and attach INF-2379 when it's ready. Alex, we'll follow up in 2 hours with the postmortem link and mitigations.
Alex_Cust: Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround :heart:
Priya: :thumbsup: Marking this slack thread for follow-up until INF-2379 is closed.
